label: tabi, tabini
title_raw: たび、たびに [たび、たびに] (tabi, tabini)
title: たび、たびに
meaning_example: Whenever I go overseas, I realize the merits of my own country.

notes.text: As far as I know, たび, means "every time". i.e. every time I get together we have a good time.
notes.html: As far as I know, たび, means "every time". i.e. every time I get together we have a good time.

notes.text:
This grammar can use past and non・past verbs in front of it. The translation is therefore slightly different: "Whenever I go" versus "Whenever I went."



V(plain form) + たび・たびに

N + の + たび・たびに
notes.html:
This grammar can use past and non・past verbs in front of it. The translation is therefore slightly different: "Whenever I go" versus "Whenever I went."

V(plain form) + たび・たびに
N + の + たび・たびに

comments.text: Generally たびに, kanji is 度
comments.html: Generally たびに, kanji is 度

comments.text: Since tense is not an important part of Japanese, you would use 行く度に(and you do not use 行った度に) and 行く度に has a strong implication that you did that in the past. How else can you say, 行く度に you did something? The sentence 日本に行く度に温泉に行きます therefore indicates that every time you visit Japan, you go to hot spring spas and you have done so in the past.

comments.text: I read in the Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese grammar that the formation for (n,vs) type verbs like 勉強するshould be 勉強度に . In that case,  サインインする度に in example # should  be   サインイン度に, shouldn't it? Please verify.
comments.html: I read in the Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese grammar that the formation for (n,vs) type verbs like 勉強するshould be 勉強度に . In that case, サインインする度に in example # should be サインイン度に, shouldn't it? Please verify.

comments.text: zep3xvii, I don't think 勉強度に is correct. 勉強する度に is correct. Therefore, サインインする度に is correct.
comments.html: zep3xvii, I don't think 勉強度に is correct. 勉強する度に is correct. Therefore, サインインする度に is correct.
